item.title: Abeno Harukas: Japan's Tallest Skyscraper View — Guide
item.description: Abeno Harukas, rising 300 metres above Tennoji, was Japan’s tallest building on its completion in 2014 and remains among the very tallest. It is a vertical city — a department store, a hotel, an art museum and offices stacked in one tower — but for visitors the draw is Harukas 300, the observation complex on the top three floors. Floor-to-ceiling glass wraps a full circuit 300 metres up, with an open-air atrium at its heart, giving a genuinely commanding view over Osaka, out to Kobe, Awaji and, on clear days, the mountains beyond.

item.title: Kyoto Tower: The City's Only Skyscraper View — Guide
item.description: Kyoto Tower, completed in 1964 and standing 131 metres directly across from Kyoto Station, is the tallest structure in a city that otherwise keeps deliberately low to protect its skyline. Its slender white form, said to evoke a lighthouse or a candle, is a divisive landmark but an unbeatable viewpoint: because Kyoto has no other tall buildings, the observation deck at 100 metres gives a genuinely uninterrupted 360-degree panorama over the whole basin, the grid of the old city, the scattered pagodas and temple roofs, and the mountains that ring it on three sides.

item.title: Ushiku Daibutsu: One of the World's Tallest Bronze Statues — Guide
item.description: Ushiku Daibutsu, standing 120 metres tall including its pedestal and lotus platform, is one of the tallest bronze statues in the world, dwarfing landmarks like the Statue of Liberty. Completed in 1993, the colossal Amida Buddha rises dramatically above the flat Ibaraki countryside, visible from a considerable distance. Visitors can enter the statue itself, riding an elevator up to an observation deck around the chest level, which offers panoramic views across the surrounding plains, alongside a small museum and garden with seasonal flower displays at the base.

item.title: Tokyo Skytree Guide: Tickets, Best Times & What's Worth It
item.description: At 634 metres, Tokyo Skytree is the tallest tower in Japan and the second-tallest structure in the world. From its observation decks, the sheer scale of the Greater Tokyo conurbation — the largest metropolitan area on Earth, home to 37 million people — spreads out in every direction until it dissolves into haze. On a clear day, Mount Fuji floats on the western horizon. It is the definitive “how big is Tokyo, really?
